issues.description: Packetization path treats any bytes payload as PCM audio and will corrupt non-audio binary frames.
issues.detail: _write_frame gates on isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray)) and fixed_audio_packet_size, so any serializer emitting non-audio bytes (control payloads, headers) gets sliced into packet_bytes chunks. The correct discriminator is frame type (AudioRawFrame), not payload type. Without a stated precondition, the contract is folklore.

issues.description: Sub-packet remainder in _audio_send_buffer is never flushed on stream end or disconnect.
issues.detail: On EndFrame, StopFrame, or disconnect the residual 0..packet_bytes-1 bytes in _audio_send_buffer are silently discarded. Trailing audio is lost with no log or signal. Either zero-pad and flush on end-of-stream, or document explicitly that sub-packet tails are dropped by design.

issues.description: fixed_audio_packet_size has byte semantics but the real concept is duration at a sample rate and width.
issues.detail: The size is an untyped integer with no enforced relationship to sample_width, channels, or sample rate. Callers must hand-compute 640 = 20ms * 16kHz * 2 bytes. A mismatched value (e.g. 641 on 16-bit mono) tears samples at every boundary and silently produces wrong-duration frames. Accept duration plus rate, or assert the invariant.

issues.description: Real-time pacing is claimed but no clock gates the send loop and existing pacing may be bypassed.
issues.detail: The PR promises real-time pacing, yet the packetization branch drains the buffer in a tight while loop with immediate await self._client.send(chunk) and returns early, skipping any _next_send_time bookkeeping. Either the existing pacing already covers this path (then say so) or it is silently broken. State and enforce the invariant.

issues.description: DTMF deserialization accepts two undocumented payload shapes instead of pinning the Vonage contract.
issues.detail: message.get('digit') or message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit') encodes uncertainty as behavior. Pick the shape the Vonage spec actually emits, log loudly on the other, and remove the fallback. Defensive 'try both' code hides protocol drift and tends to survive forever.

issues.description: Comments assert 16-bit linear PCM but nothing enforces sample format or width.
issues.detail: serialize/deserialize comments claim PCM16, yet no check on frame.format or sample width exists. If upstream hands 8-bit or float audio, the resampler chews garbage and ships it. A one-line assert or explicit precondition beats a comment, and would prevent silent malformed output.

synthesis.summary: The panel reaches consensus that the Vonage serializer is roughly the right shape but the FastAPIWebsocketTransport packetization path is too eager and under-specified. The dominant correctness concern is that _write_frame treats any bytes payload as PCM, will corrupt non-audio binary, drops sub-packet tails on stream end, and ships under a 'real-time pacing' banner with no clock or invariant tying packet emission to wall-clock time. Secondary concerns: fixed_audio_packet_size encodes duration as raw bytes with no enforced relationship to sample rate or width, DTMF parsing hedges across two undocumented Vonage shapes, and PCM16 is asserted in comments but never checked. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — gate packetization on frame type, define and enforce the size/duration invariant, flush tails on end-of-stream, and pin the DTMF schema before merge.
